adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts (lines 72-91), the code directly calls fetch() to refresh tokens without wrapping it in refreshOAuthTokens(). Other calendar services like Google, Office365, Zoom, etc. all wrap their refresh token calls with refreshOAuthTokens() to support credential sharing mode. Salesforce's implementation bypasses this pattern entirely - it directly posts to 'https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token' with the local refresh_token. This means when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is configured, Salesforce will still use local refresh tokens instead of the sync endpoint, which is inconsistent with the credential sharing feature being implemented.
